intro: Answer every question. You may use a calculator. Show your working for calculations. The 6-mark question is marked on how well you link your ideas together.

questions.q: A compound has one magnesium atom for every two chlorine atoms. What is its formula?
questions.ms: Answer: C: MgCl₂. B1.

questions.q: What is the simplest ratio of hydrogen atoms to oxygen atoms in hydrogen peroxide, H₂O₂?
questions.ms: Answer: B: 1 : 1. B1.

questions.q: Which metal must be extracted from its ore by electrolysis?
questions.ms: Answer: D: Aluminium. B1.

questions.q: What does a catalyst do?
options: Speeds up a reaction and gets used up
Speeds up a reaction without being used up
Changes the products of a reaction
questions.ms: Answer: B. B1.

questions.q: Which metals are used in a catalytic converter?
questions.ms: Answer: A. B1.

questions.q:
Balance these equations. Type them with normal numbers, for example 2H2 + O2 → 2H2O.
Mg + O₂ → MgO
questions.ms: Answer: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO. B1.

questions.q: Fe₂O₃ + CO → Fe + CO₂
questions.ms: Answer: Fe₂O₃ + 3CO → 2Fe + 3CO₂. B1 for 2Fe. B1 for 3CO and 3CO₂.

questions.q: Na + H₂O → NaOH + H₂
questions.ms: Answer: 2Na + 2H₂O → 2NaOH + H₂. B1.

questions.q:
Calcium carbonate breaks down when heated: CaCO₃ → CaO + CO₂
Calculate the mass of calcium oxide made from 25 g of calcium carbonate. (g)
questions.ms: Answer: 14 g. M1 for M<sub>r</sub> CaO = 56 (and CaCO₃ = 100). M1 for 25 ÷ 100 × 56 (or 100 g → 56 g, scaled). A1 for 14 g.

questions.q:
Magnesium burns in oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
Calculate the mass of magnesium oxide made from 6 g of magnesium. (g)
questions.ms: Answer: 10 g. M1 for 2 × 24 = 48 and 2 × 40 = 80. M1 for 6 ÷ 48 × 80. A1 for 10 g.

questions.q:
In a reaction, the theoretical yield is 10.0 g. The student actually makes 8.5 g of product.
Calculate the percentage yield. (%)
Give two reasons why the actual yield is less than the theoretical yield.
questions.ms: Answer: Any two: some product is lost when transferring or filtering; the reaction may not go to completion; side reactions make other products; some reactant is lost or impure.. B1 each, up to 2.

questions.q: Explain why gold is found as the pure metal in the ground, but iron is found as iron oxide.
questions.ms: Answer: Gold is very unreactive (at the bottom of the reactivity series), so it does not react with oxygen. Iron is more reactive, so it has reacted with oxygen to form a compound.. B1 gold is unreactive / low in the reactivity series. B1 iron is more reactive so it reacts with oxygen (forms compounds).

questions.q: Zinc is added to copper sulfate solution. What happens?
options: Zinc displaces copper, because zinc is more reactive
No reaction, because zinc is less reactive
questions.ms: Answer: A. B1.

questions.q: Copper is added to magnesium sulfate solution. What happens?
options: No reaction, because copper is less reactive than magnesium
Magnesium metal forms on the copper
The solution turns blue straight away
questions.ms: Answer: B. B1.

questions.q: Write a word equation for the reaction in 14(a).
questions.ms: Answer: zinc + copper sulfate → zinc sulfate + copper. B1.

questions.q: Explain how a catalytic converter makes car exhaust gases less harmful. Name the harmful gases and what they are changed into.
questions.ms: Answer: It contains platinum/palladium/rhodium catalysts on a honeycomb with a large surface area. Carbon monoxide → carbon dioxide; nitrogen oxides → nitrogen (and oxygen); unburnt hydrocarbons → carbon dioxide and water.. B1 contains catalysts (Pt, Pd, Rh) / speeds up reactions. B1 CO → CO₂. B1 nitrogen oxides → nitrogen. B1 unburnt hydrocarbons → CO₂ + H₂O, or honeycomb gives a large surface area.

questions.q:
A student heats different masses of magnesium in a crucible and measures the mass of magnesium oxide made.
Mass of magnesium (g)0.120.240.360.480.60
Mass of magnesium oxide (g)0.200.400.480.801.00

Which mass of magnesium gave the anomalous result? (g)
questions.ms: Answer: 0.36 g (it should give about 0.60 g of oxide). B1.

questions.q: Suggest a reason for the anomalous result.
questions.ms: Answer: Not heated for long enough so not all the magnesium reacted, or some magnesium oxide smoke escaped when the lid was lifted.. B1 for a sensible reason.

questions.q: Name the independent variable and the dependent variable.
questions.ms: Answer: Independent: mass of magnesium. Dependent: mass of magnesium oxide.. B1 each.

questions.q: Describe the relationship between the mass of magnesium and the mass of magnesium oxide.
questions.ms: Answer: As the mass of magnesium increases, the mass of magnesium oxide increases. It is directly proportional: doubling the magnesium doubles the oxide (oxide ≈ 1.67 × magnesium).. B1 positive relationship. B1 directly proportional with evidence (doubling) or the multiplier.

questions.q: Which type of graph should she draw for these results?
options: Line graph (scatter with a line of best fit)
questions.ms: Answer: B. B1. Both variables are continuous.

questions.q:
Copper is extracted by heating copper oxide with carbon. Aluminium is extracted from aluminium oxide by electrolysis.
Explain why the two metals are extracted in different ways, and compare the two methods.
questions.ms: Answer: Level 3 answer points: reactivity series; carbon is more reactive than copper, so it can remove oxygen from copper oxide (reduction / displacement); aluminium is more reactive than carbon, so carbon cannot reduce it; electrolysis breaks down molten aluminium oxide using electricity; electrolysis needs a lot of energy to melt the ore and run the current, so it is expensive; heating with carbon is cheaper; carbon method makes carbon dioxide.. Level-marked. Level 3 (5–6): explains both methods using the position of carbon in the reactivity series, and compares cost/energy. Level 2 (3–4): explains one method clearly and makes a comparison. Level 1 (1–2): simple statements such as 'aluminium is more reactive'.
